paragraphs.text: FRONT-END ENGINEERING DESIGN (FEED)
100 t/d Sulfuric Acid Plant — DCDA / Elemental Sulfur
EMERGENCY PROCEDURES
Emergency Response and Recovery — Setpoint & Response Time Consistency Verified
This document contains automated consistency status flags. Parameters marked FAIL require engineering review before progression to Detailed Engineering.
🚨  EMERGENCY: EMERGENCY 1 — AUTOMATIC ESD ACTUATION (any SIF trip)

E1.1.1  [CRO]  Confirm ESD actuation on DCS: identify which SIF has tripped (SIS trip log on dedicated SIS screen). Announce on plant PA: "ESD actuation — all field personnel muster at [muster point]."
E1.1.2  [CRO]  Confirm that SDV-E01 (sulfur block) is CLOSED (position feedback on DCS). If position feedback shows OPEN, escalate to MANUAL ESD.
Verify: SDV-E01 "Closed" confirmation on DCS position indicator
E1.1.3  [CRO]  Confirm K-301A (air blower) continues running — air purge of furnace is ESSENTIAL post-ESD. Air flow FT-201 > 4,000 Nm³/h must be maintained.
Verify: FT-201 > 4,000 Nm³/h on DCS
E1.1.4  [Shift Supervisor]  Account for all personnel at muster point within 5 minutes of PA announcement.
Verify: All persons signed in to shift accounted for at muster
E1.1.5  [CRO]  Monitor TT-201 (furnace temperature). Confirm trend downward. If temperature rises after ESD, contact Process Engineer immediately — potential ignition source remaining.
Verify: TT-201 trending down within 3 minutes
🚨  EMERGENCY: EMERGENCY 2 — MAJOR SO₂ RELEASE / TOXIC GAS CLOUD

rows: Sulfur gun blockage → rich burn; air flow loss; refractory degradation
Check TT-201 trend: if still rising after ESD, evacuate 50 m radius and contact fire service. If declining: investigate root cause (check FT-201, AT-202 O₂, sulfur gun condition).
TT-201 < 200°C; root cause identified and corrected; HAZOP closeout of trip event; Shift Supervisor sign-off
Air blower surge; outlet duct blockage; stack damper closed unintentionally
CHECK XV-E04 stack damper position: if CLOSED (pre-correction FAIL state), open manually at field — this is urgent. After correction: investigate duct blockage.
Stack damper open; duct clear; furnace pressure < −10 mbar before restart
BFW pump failure; LCV-201 failure closed; large steam demand spike
Start standby BFW pump P-201B immediately. Set LIC-201 to manual — maximum BFW demand. Do not reduce steam demand until drum level recovers to 30%.
LT-201 > 40%; BFW pump confirmed duty/standby operational; LIC-201 3-element control verified
Steam export trip; PCV-202 failure closed; excessive steam generation
Open steam dump to atmosphere via manual bypass valve (PV-202-bypass) if available. Reduce BFW if steam generation continues rising. DO NOT vent to atmosphere without HSE notification.
PT-202 < 42 barg stable; PCV-202 operation verified
Plant operating at 110% surge load — this is the DESIGN FAIL scenario. Temperature reached trip setpoint.

Confirm ESD actuation; reduce to 0% load; investigate root cause (confirm this is the design deficiency — bed height issue — per H&MB and SRS records). Do NOT attempt restart at 110% load until process design corrected.
Process design corrected per H&MB FAIL resolution; restart only at ≤100% load until redesign is implemented and validated
Catalyst degradation; absorption tower acid concentration low; IPAT/FAT pump failure
CHECK AT-501/502 acid concentration. If < 97.5 wt%, dilution water fault (check FCV-501/502). If acid OK, investigate catalyst performance (check all converter pass temperatures).
AT-403 < 400 mg/Nm³ stable; root cause identified; CEMS download for regulatory review
Dispatch pump failure; tanker not available; over-production

Stop all product transfer from absorption to storage (close product transfer valve). Halt dispatching only if dispatch pump is failed — not if tanker is absent (continue dispatching). Contact dispatch coordinator immediately.
LT-701 < 70% before resuming production; dispatch pump confirmed operational

paragraphs.text: E2.1  [CRO]  On AA-901-HH (25 ppm): manually initiate TOTAL PLANT ESD via Control Room ESD button if automatic ESD has not actuated. Confirm PA system active.
Verify: Plant ESD confirmed; PA evacuation announcement active
E2.2  [Shift Supervisor]  Account for all personnel. Any person exposed to SO₂ > 5 ppm: escort to fresh air, administer O₂ if available, arrange medical assessment.
Verify: All personnel accounted for; no personnel in toxic zone
E2.3  [CRO]  Identify source: check if release is from furnace/converter (SO₂ gas) or from acid system (acid mist/SO₃). This determines the response priority.
Verify: Source identified from F&G node activation pattern on DCS F&G map
E2.4  [CRO]  Confirm K-301A continues running for air purge. Confirm AT-403 (CEMS) recording for regulatory evidence.
Verify: AT-403 recording; CEMS data logger confirmed active

rows: CRO announces PA warning: "SO₂ warning — upwind personnel stay clear of [affected area]." Investigate source immediately.
AUTOMATIC ESD actuation + PA EVACUATION alarm. All non-essential personnel evacuate to upwind muster point. Emergency services: DIAL [site emergency number].
Indicates large release. Full site evacuation. Contact emergency services, site EHS Manager, and notify relevant Local Authority.
Report to CRO immediately; CRO initiates PA warning; manual ESD if required.
Flush immediately with copious water for minimum 20 minutes. Call site first-aider. Hospital evaluation for all acid exposures regardless of apparent severity.

heading.text: E2.2 SO₂ Exposure Limits (for field response planning)

paragraphs.text: 🚨  EMERGENCY: EMERGENCY 3 — SULFURIC ACID MAJOR SPILL

rows: SCBA — entry ONLY with trained team
Extreme hazard; NO ENTRY without full SCBA and buddy system

paragraphs.text: ⛔ DANGER: CONCENTRATED H₂SO₄ REACTS VIOLENTLY WITH WATER. NEVER add water directly to spilled acid. Only use water mist from a safe distance (>3 m). Risk of spattering and steam explosion if water is poured onto concentrated acid.
E3.1  [CRO]  On notification of major acid spill: initiate production shutdown (reduce to 0% load immediately — do not wait for ESD). Confirm SDV-E05 (product block) CLOSED.
Verify: SDV-E05 closed; production load at 0%
E3.2  [Shift Supervisor]  Confirm bund isolation valve for affected tank area is CLOSED. Confirm bund is containing the spill.
Verify: Visual confirmation from safe distance; CCTV if available
E3.3  [Field Operator (SCBA)]  If safe to do so: position spill response foam/neutralisation equipment at bund perimeter (outside bund). Do NOT enter bund without emergency team leader approval.
E3.4  [Shift Supervisor]  Initiate site emergency muster. Notify EHS Manager and site emergency coordinator.
Verify: All personnel at muster; emergency coordinator contacted
🚨  EMERGENCY: EMERGENCY 4 — LOSS OF INSTRUMENT AIR

rows: Contain with dry sand/earth. Do NOT use water on concentrated H₂SO₄ (violent exotherm). PPE: face shield, acid gloves, acid apron. Recover with absorbent material.
Activate spill kit. Ensure bund valve closed. Dilute carefully with water spray (fine mist from distance). Neutralise with Na₂CO₃ or lime slurry ONLY after initial containment.
EHS Manager + regulatory notification within 24 h
ACTIVATE SITE EMERGENCY PLAN. Evacuate downwind area. Contact fire service. Do NOT approach without full chemical protection suit + SCBA. Contain within bund — verify bund isolation valve CLOSED.
Immediate notification to Environment Agency, Local Authority, and HSE within 1 hour

paragraphs.text: Loss of instrument air (IA pressure < 5 barg) causes all pneumatic control valves to move to their fail-safe positions simultaneously. This is a significant process disturbance. The fail-safe positions defined in the C&E matrix (Doc 6) are:
E4.1  [CRO]  Check IA supply pressure PT-IA-001. If < 5 barg: confirm IA compressor K-901 status. Start standby compressor if available.
Verify: K-901B running; IA pressure recovering
E4.2  [CRO]  Monitor all valve positions via DCS: confirm fail-safe positions per table above. Note any valve NOT in expected fail-safe position — this indicates a valve actuator fault.
Verify: All fail-safe positions confirmed via DCS position feedback

E4.3  [CRO]  If IA not restored within 10 minutes: initiate controlled shutdown Procedure 3 (Planned Shutdown Phase 1 onwards). Do not attempt to hold plant on manual override beyond 10 minutes without IA.
Verify: Shutdown procedure initiated; Shift Supervisor notified
🚨  EMERGENCY: EMERGENCY 5 — POWER FAILURE (TOTAL ELECTRICAL)

rows: Sulfur feed stops — furnace temperature drops
Monitor TT-201 declining. If IA restored within 5 min, restart sulfur gradually from Governor setpoint. If > 5 min, initiate controlled shutdown.
Maximum BFW flow to WHB — risk of drum overfill
Set LIC-201 to manual/override. Monitor LT-201. If drum > 80%, close BFW isolation manually.
Dilution water stops — acid concentration rises
Monitor AT-501/502. If concentration > 98.8 wt%, manually adjust dilution water bypass valve.
Maximum CW to acid cooler — acid cools below target
Non-critical; temperature will recover when IA restored.
Confirm ESD actuation on SIS panel. If ESD trips, follow E1 procedure.
UPS activates for DCS, SIS, F&G, emergency lighting. All MV motors (blower, BFW pump) coast to stop.
CRO: Confirm DCS alive on UPS. Confirm SIS alive — all SIFs remain armed. PA announcement: "Power failure — all personnel muster."
K-301A air blower coasts to stop — no air purge. Furnace without air and sulfur (FCV-101 fails closed).
Furnace is dark — no ignition, no combustion. Key risk: residual SO₂ in system. Do NOT attempt manual restart of blower until DG is confirmed live.
Emergency diesel generator (DG) should energise MV bus.
CRO: Confirm DG has picked up MV bus. Restart K-301A on DG supply immediately for purge airflow. Confirm BFW pump P-201B available on DG.
DG running; air purge active. Plant is in safe shutdown state.
Maintain air purge. Monitor WHB drum level. Do NOT restart sulfur until utility power is restored and root cause identified.
WHB will lose pressure; acid circuit may begin to cool and risk solidification in low spots.
Process Engineer decision: drain acid circuits if power restoration not expected within 2 hours. Follow Planned Shutdown Steps S.8–S.10.
Action Required Before Procedures Can Be Relied Upon
SIF-05 will trip on every 110% surge operation — not a genuine emergency but a design deficiency
Resolve Pass 1 temperature (H&MB FAIL). Until resolved, 110% operation is PROHIBITED and this emergency procedure for SIF-05 is a routine event procedure.
Stack damper XV-E04 Fail Closed during ESD blocks venting — manual compensating measure required
Correct valve to Fail Open (C&E FAIL). Until corrected, add mandatory manual field step to open damper within 60 s of ESD in this procedure.
F&G area monitors: threshold setpoints (5 ppm HIGH; 25 ppm HH) confirmed consistent with occupational exposure limits (WEL) and IDLH values
Bund sizing (110% of tank volume) confirmed per BoD environmental design criteria
All fail-safe positions confirmed consistent with C&E matrix Doc 6
No action — verify at FAT testing
DG transfer time and air blower restart timing needs dynamic simulation validation
Confirm DG auto-start time < 30 s; confirm blower coast-down time to confirm purge interruption duration
SIS trip setpoints in procedures match SRS Doc 8 and C&E Doc 6

Verify: Shutdown procedure initiated; Shift Supervisor notified
